intro: Nursing assistants give hands-on care every shift, the foundation for many health care careers. The closest of the 25 careers below is Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses, with a 91% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,400, which is 52% more than the $42,260 nursing assistants earn.
why_it_works: Helping patients bathe, move and eat means noticing small changes and reporting them before they become emergencies. O*NET rates service orientation at 4 out of 5 for this job and social perceptiveness at 3.62. Nursing, therapy and emergency care build on that same care. Most matches need no new degree, though nursing licenses take some training. The gaps include persuasion and negotiation.
tips: Ask your employer about tuition help for LPN or RN programs; many hospitals pay for it.
Occupational Therapy Assistants earn $72,300, which is 71% more, after an associate program.
Keep a list of the units and patients you have cared for; it helps in nursing school applications.

faq.q: What jobs can former nursing assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are licensed practical nurses (91%), Registered Nurses (84%) and Occupational Therapy Assistants (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Paramedics are also 82% matched and earn $60,600, which is 43% more than the $42,260 nursing assistant median.

faq.q: Which careers for nursing assistants pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Registered Nurses earn $97,550 (131% more), Respiratory Therapists $82,280 (95% more) and Occupational Therapy Assistants $72,300 (71% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Registered nursing usually requires a degree and a state license.

faq.q: Do nursing assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: For some paths. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than assistants already have, but nursing roles need a license. Registered nursing usually needs a bachelor's degree, held by 56% of workers in a close match, though associate degree programs also lead to the license.

faq.q: What skills should nursing assistants learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are persuasion, negotiation, operation and control and operations analysis. Coordination already rates 3.12 out of 5 for nursing assistants in O*NET, so clinical training and running equipment are the main steps toward nursing or therapy roles.
